claims.claim:
Incident SW point of the Hole in the Wall, Abaco near the SW point of the Hole in the Wall, Abaco (29th of
April)
claims.citation: New York Herald, 1 June 1866, p. 8, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Bolivian, Couche, from Liverpool for New Or-
leans, with a cargo of hardware, rice, &c, got ashore near
the SW point of the Hole in the Wall, Abaco, on the 29th of
April. After throwing overboard a portion of her cargo she
got off on the 30th, and proceeded on her voyage. The cargo
thrown overboard has been taken to Nassau by sundry
wrecking vessels. (The B arrived at New Orleans May 5, [cut]
and has sailed again.)

claims.claim: Incident SW point of Abaco near the SW point of Abaco (April 29)
claims.citation: New York Herald, 15 June 1866, p. 8, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
April 29 (not previously reported)—Steamship Bolivian
(Br), Couch, from Liverpool for New Orleans, with passen-
gers and a general cargo; ashore near the SW point of Abaco;
threw over part of cargo, got off and proceeded; much of the
jetsoned cargo was taken by wreckers to Nassau and sold by
Admiralty as derelict.
